summary: Show the globe and its projected plane at once so distortion becomes something measured rather than described.
objective: Build a globe and a projection surface where I can compare shapes, areas and distances between the angular and the planar coordinate frames.
intent_signals: Show how a map projection distorts shape and area.
Compare geographic coordinates with a projected coordinate system.
example_prompts: Build a globe with a projection surface and comparison patches that show distortion.
Show a great-circle route and its projected path on the same screen.
negative_signals: Not a geodesy toolkit: datum transformations and their accuracy are outside this recipe.
Not a claim about any specific dataset or projection parameter set unless the scene states it.
not_for: Not a geodesy toolkit: datum transformations and their accuracy are outside this recipe.
Not a claim about any specific dataset or projection parameter set unless the scene states it.

entities.name: Globe and graticule
entities.guidance: Model the globe with a real graticule and named reference features, since a projection is a mapping of those features.

entities.name: Projection surface
entities.guidance: Two optional planar views for spherical plate carree and spherical Mercator; they are mathematical coordinate maps, not claims of literal ray projection onto a cylinder.

entities.name: Comparison patches
entities.guidance: Place equal-area or equal-shape test patches at several latitudes and report their projected measurements.

state_contract.model: Authored spherical teaching model with R=6371000 m as a chosen rounded radius, not an ellipsoid or survey datum. Angles are radians internally; central meridian lambda0=0 and zero false easting/northing. Offer spherical plate carree x=R wrap(lambda-lambda0), y=R phi, and spherical Mercator x=R wrap(lambda-lambda0), y=R ln(tan(pi/4+phi/2)), with wrap in [-pi,pi). Both display only |phi|<=85 degrees, an authored common comparison window; Mercator poles are outside its mathematical domain. Split curves and polygons at the antimeridian and clip at the window, never connect across a seam. Globe coordinates are R(cos(phi)cos(lambda),cos(phi)sin(lambda),sin(phi)). A patch is a geodesic disk of fixed radius ell=100000 m: for center unit c and local orthonormal tangent vectors e1,e2, its boundary is R[cos(ell/R)c+sin(ell/R)(e1 cos(t)+e2 sin(t))], t in [0,2pi). Moving c rigidly relocates the same disk; its spherical area is 2 pi R^2[1-cos(ell/R)]. For route endpoint unit vectors u,v use sigma=atan2(|u cross v|,u dot v) and distance R sigma. For 0<sigma<pi the great-circle arc is R[sin((1-s)sigma)u+sin(s sigma)v]/sin(sigma), 0<=s<=1; coincident endpoints give zero distance and a point, antipodal/near-antipodal endpoints are reported as requiring a route-plane choice and are not interpolated. Near-coincident arcs may use normalized linear interpolation labeled approximate. Planar route lengths and polygon areas are sampled estimates with display resolution and refinement differences shown; they are not spherical measurements.
state_contract.authority: The angular coordinates are authoritative; projected coordinates are derived. A measurement without a stated frame and unit is not a result.
actions: Move a test patch to a different latitude.
Toggle the graticule and the geodesic route.

invariants: Every reported measurement names its frame and unit; angular degrees are never compared directly with linear metres.
Test patches keep their identity across projections so their distortion can be compared.
A geodesic route on the globe and its projected image are shown as the same route, not as two independent curves.
A test patch keeps its intrinsic ground dimensions as it moves in latitude, so any change in its projected size is distortion rather than a change of the patch itself.
Each projection declares its valid domain, seam and pole treatment; positions outside that domain are reported rather than wrapped silently.
motion_guidance: A morph between globe and map is optional and labeled a display interpolation, without assigning measurement meaning to intermediate poses.
Move patches slowly across latitudes so the growth or shear of the projected patch is legible.
known_limits: Only the two stated spherical mappings and the common 85-degree display window are implemented; no ellipsoidal datum transformations or surveying accuracy.
The rounded sphere radius is an authored teaching choice; changing to an ellipsoid requires different projection and geodesic formulas.

Spherical formulas are written in the model and referenced to PROJ documentation; geometric patch and great-circle constructions are authored analytic choices. Sampled planar measurements expose their resolution and clipping status.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: Geographic coordinate systems are based on a three-dimensional ellipsoidal or spherical surface with locations defined by angular measurements, while projected coordinate systems are planar and use linear measurements for coordinates.
claims.scope: Standard GIS definitions as stated in the cited vendor documentation.

source_refs.locator: Coordinate systems, map projections, and transformations, geographic and projected definitions

claims.statement: There is no way to transpose a curved surface to a flat surface without some distortion, so projections make different compromises: some preserve area, others preserve local angles, and others preserve specific distances or directions.
claims.scope: General property of map projections as cited; which property a given projection preserves must be stated per projection.

source_refs.locator: Coordinate systems, map projections, and transformations, distortion and compromises

claims.statement: The spherical Mercator forward map uses x=k0 R lambda and y=k0 R ln(tan(pi/4+phi/2)); spherical equidistant cylindrical coordinates use longitude scaled by the cosine of the standard parallel and latitude offset from the origin. With zero standard parallel and origin, plate carree has x=R lambda and y=R phi in linear units.
claims.scope: Spherical forward formulas with longitude relative to the central meridian. This recipe chooses k0=1 and zero standard parallel/origin; its radius and 85-degree display crop are authored parameters, not measured accuracy claims.

object_craft.structure: A sphere of the declared model radius with graticule, reference meridian and labeled reference points; seams and clipped polar regions remain visible.
object_craft.material: Matte globe with high-contrast graticule; keep the surface unlit enough that projected overlays stay readable.
object_craft.articulation: The globe rotates for viewing only; coordinates are never changed by camera motion.

object_craft.structure: Fixed intrinsic-radius geodesic disks with center marks and local tangent axes in both views; clipped patches are labeled and are not used for whole-patch area comparison.
object_craft.material: Identical patch material in both views so any visual difference is genuinely geometric.
object_craft.articulation: Patches are re-projected whenever the projection or their position changes.

physical_contract.scope: Spherical coordinate transformation and analytic/sampled geometric measurements; no ellipsoidal, terrain or hydrological model.
checks: Every readout states its frame and units.
Switching projections preserves patch identity and updates all measurements.
